docs.title: vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix
docs.text: vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix is an MkDocs plugin. It lets you keep numeric prefixes such as 010-- in your Markdown filenames and folder names, so the files sort in the order you want, and removes those prefixes from the URLs and output paths of the built site.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
You write your sources like this:

docs/
├── index.md
├── 010--introduction.md
├── 020--getting-started.md
└── 030--guides/
    ├── 010--setup.md
    └── 020--deployment.md

The plugin is registered under the name strip-number-prefix. With it enabled, MkDocs writes the site like this:

site/
├── index.html
├── introduction/index.html
├── getting-started/index.html
└── guides/
    ├── setup/index.html
    └── deployment/index.html

The source files on disk are not renamed. Only the output path (dest_path) and the page URL (url) that MkDocs uses for each page change.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Clean URLs. A regular expression (default ^\d+--) is removed from every path component of every documentation page.
  • Ordering stays in the filenames. Prefixes still control the order in which MkDocs discovers files and sorts the automatic navigation.
  • Collision detection. If two files would end up at the same clean path, the build stops (strict: true, the default) or the plugin logs a warning and leaves both files at their prefixed paths (strict: false).
  • Navigation titles. Section titles derived from prefixed folder names, such as 030 guides, are cleaned to guides (strip_nav_titles, on by default).
  • Optional link rewriting. strip_links: true rewrites .md link targets in the Markdown before MkDocs renders it. Read Links and navigation before turning it on.

docs.title: This site uses the plugin
docs.text: The source of this documentation lives in src_docs/md/ of the repository, and every page except this one has a numeric prefix, for example src_docs/md/010--installation.md. The page is published at installation/, not at 010--installation/. The configuration is in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 or later (requires-python = ">=3.9" in pyproject.toml).
  • MkDocs 1.5.0 or later (the only runtime dependency is mkdocs>=1.5.0). CI tests the plugin against MkDocs 1.5.x and 1.6.x. This documentation site is built with ProperDocs 1.6.7, which loads MkDocs plugins unchanged.

docs.title: License
docs.text: MIT. The source is at github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The plugin is published on PyPI as vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix. The import package is mkdocs_strip_number_prefix, and the MkDocs plugin name is strip-number-prefix.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.9 or later.
  • MkDocs 1.5.0 or later. Installing the plugin pulls in mkdocs>=1.5.0 if it is missing.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
uvpipuvx (no install) 
uv pip install --upgrade vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix

python -m pip install --upgrade vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix

Run MkDocs with the plugin in a throwaway environment:

uvx --from mkdocs --with vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix mkdocs build

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
To use the latest commit from the main branch:

python -m pip install git+https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix

To work on the plugin itself, clone the repository and install it in editable mode with the development extras:

git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix
cd vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

The dev extra installs pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-mock, pyyaml, ruff, black, mypy and pre-commit. See Development.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
1. Print the installed version:

    python -c "import mkdocs_strip_number_prefix as m; print(m.__version__)"

    The version comes from the git tag the package was built from. A source checkout without the generated _version.py file reports 0.0.0+unknown.

  2. Confirm that MkDocs can find the plugin. The package registers this entry point in the mkdocs.plugins group:

    [project.entry-points."mkdocs.plugins"]
strip-number-prefix = "mkdocs_strip_number_prefix.plugin:StripNumberPrefixPlugin"

    If MkDocs reports The "strip-number-prefix" plugin is not installed, the plugin is installed in a different Python environment from the one that runs mkdocs. Install both into the same environment.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with the Quickstart.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walk-through builds a small MkDocs site with prefixed filenames and checks that the output URLs are clean.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The plugin and MkDocs are installed in the same environment. See Installation.
  • An empty working folder.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the source folder and three pages:

    mkdir -p docs/030--guides
printf '# Home\n\nRead the [introduction](010--introduction.md).\n' > docs/index.md
printf '# Introduction\n\nNext: [setup](030--guides/010--setup.md).\n' > docs/010--introduction.md
printf '# Setup\n\nBack to the [introduction](../010--introduction.md).\n' > docs/030--guides/010--setup.md

  2. Create mkdocs.yml next to the docs folder:

    site_name: Prefix demo
plugins:
  - search
  - strip-number-prefix

    Listing strip-number-prefix without options uses the defaults: pattern: '^\d+--', strict: true, strip_links: false, strip_nav_titles: true, verbose: false, dry_run: false.

  3. Build the site:

    mkdocs build --strict

    The build finishes without warnings. The links in step 1 point at the prefixed source files, and MkDocs resolves them to the clean URLs.

  4. List the generated pages:

    find site -name index.html | sort

    Result:

    site/guides/setup/index.html
site/index.html
site/introduction/index.html

    No 010-- or 030-- appears in the output paths.

  5. Look at a link in the home page:

    grep -o 'href="introduction/"' site/index.html

    The link written as 010--introduction.md was rendered as introduction/.

docs.title: What happened
docs.text:
• MkDocs collected index.md, 010--introduction.md and 030--guides/010--setup.md from docs/.
  • In its on_files step, the plugin removed 010-- and 030-- from each path component and set the new dest_path and url of each file.
  • MkDocs converted each Markdown link that names a source file into the URL of that file, so the links follow the clean URLs automatically.
  • In the navigation, the folder 030--guides became the section guides.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Change the prefix format or turn on collision warnings: Configuration.
  • Learn the link rules: Links and navigation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All options go under the plugin entry in mkdocs.yml. This is the full list with the defaults defined in StripNumberPrefixPlugin.config_scheme:

plugins:
  - strip-number-prefix:
      pattern: '^\d+--'
      strict: true
      strip_links: false
      strip_nav_titles: true
      verbose: false
      dry_run: false
Option Type Default Effect pattern string ^\d+-- Regular expression that marks the prefix. strict boolean true Stop the build when two pages map to the same clean path. strip_links boolean false Rewrite .md link targets in the Markdown source. strip_nav_titles boolean true Remove prefixes from navigation titles. verbose boolean false Log each transformation at INFO level. dry_run boolean false Log what would change and leave paths, titles and links untouched.

docs.title: pattern
docs.text:
A Python regular expression. It is compiled once, in the on_config step. For every documentation page, the plugin splits the source path into its components (folders and the filename) and, for each component that the pattern matches at the start (re.match), removes the matched text.

Example with the default ^\d+--:

Source path Output URL 010--intro.md intro/ 030--guides/020--deploy.md guides/deploy/ guides/020--deploy.md guides/deploy/ faq.md faq/

Quote the pattern in single quotes

In YAML, write pattern: '^\d+--'. Inside single quotes a backslash is a literal character, so the regular expression receives ^\d+--. If you write '^\\d+--', the regular expression receives two backslashes and matches a literal backslash followed by d, so nothing is stripped.

An invalid expression stops the build with a PluginError:

Invalid regex pattern '<pattern>': <reason>

More formats are in Prefix patterns.

docs.title: strict
docs.text:
Two pages collide when they have the same path after the prefix is removed, for example 010--intro.md and 020--intro.md (both become intro.md).

  • strict: true (default): the build stops with StripNumberPrefix: Multiple files would map to 'intro.md': 010--intro.md, 020--intro.md.
  • strict: false: the plugin logs the same message as a warning and does not clean the colliding pages. They stay at 010--intro/ and 020--intro/. Pages that do not collide are cleaned as usual.

See Edge cases and troubleshooting.

docs.title: strip_links
docs.text:
When true, the plugin rewrites Markdown links of the form [text](path.md) or [text](path.md#anchor) before MkDocs renders the page. It removes the prefix from the filename only, not from folder names.

Leave strip_links off in most projects

MkDocs resolves a link by matching it against the source path of a file, which still contains the prefix. A rewritten link such as intro.md no longer matches 010--intro.md, so MkDocs reports the target is not found among documentation files and leaves the link unresolved. With the default strip_links: false, links to the prefixed filenames work and point at the clean URLs.

Details: Links and navigation.

docs.title: strip_nav_titles
docs.text:
When true (default), the plugin walks the navigation in its on_nav step and cleans titles that start with a prefix. It recognises two forms:

  • A title that matches pattern, such as 010--intro. The prefix is removed, -- is removed and each remaining - becomes a space: intro.
  • A title that starts with digits followed by whitespace, such as 030 guides. This is the form MkDocs produces from a folder named 030--guides. The digits and spaces are removed: guides.

Titles you set yourself in nav: and titles taken from a page's first heading normally contain no prefix and are left as they are.

docs.title: verbose
docs.text:
When true, the plugin logs each path change, title change and rewritten link at INFO level through the Python logger mkdocs_strip_number_prefix.plugin.

Note

MkDocs only prints messages from loggers under the mkdocs namespace. The plugin's own logger is outside it, so in a normal mkdocs build these INFO messages are not printed, even with mkdocs build -v. Warnings from the plugin (non-strict collisions) are printed without the usual WARNING - prefix.

docs.title: dry_run
docs.text: When true, the plugin still detects collisions, but for every page it would change it logs a DRY RUN: Would transform ... message instead of changing dest_path and url. Navigation titles and links are also left unchanged. The site is built with the prefixed URLs. The same logging limitation as for verbose applies.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
site_name: My documentation
theme:
  name: material
plugins:
  - search
  - strip-number-prefix:
      pattern: '^\d{3}--'
      strict: true
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Introduction: 010--introduction.md
  - Guides:
      - Setup: 020--guides/010--setup.md

nav: entries always name the source paths, including prefixes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The plugin is a single class, StripNumberPrefixPlugin, in src/mkdocs_strip_number_prefix/plugin.py. It subclasses MkDocs' BasePlugin and implements four MkDocs events. This page follows one file, 030--guides/010--setup.md, through a build with the default options.

docs.title: The three paths of a page
docs.text:
MkDocs keeps three related values for every file:

Attribute Meaning Example before Changed by the plugin? src_path Where MkDocs reads the source on disk 030--guides/010--setup.md No dest_path Where the HTML is written inside site_dir 030--guides/010--setup/index.html Yes url The URL used in links, navigation and the sitemap 030--guides/010--setup/ Yes

src_path must stay unchanged. If it were cleaned, MkDocs would look for guides/setup.md on disk and fail with FileNotFoundError. An early version of the plugin did exactly that; the changelog lists the fix.

docs.title: 1. on_config: compile the pattern
docs.text: The value of pattern is compiled with re.compile. If compilation fails, the plugin raises PluginError("Invalid regex pattern ...") and the build stops before any file is read.

docs.title: 2. on_files: compute and apply clean paths
docs.text:
This is where the URLs change. The step has three passes.

Pass 1: collect. For each file where is_documentation_page() is true (Markdown pages; images, CSS and other assets are skipped), the plugin splits src_path into components and removes the prefix from each component that the pattern matches:

030--guides/010--setup.md
   │            │
   ▼            ▼
guides   /   setup.md        → virtual clean path: guides/setup.md

Only files whose clean path differs from src_path are kept for the next passes. index.md and other unprefixed files are not touched.

Pass 2: detect collisions. The clean paths are grouped. If two or more source files share one clean path, the plugin records a collision:

  • with strict: true it raises PluginError("StripNumberPrefix: Multiple files would map to ...");
  • with strict: false it logs the same text as a warning.

Pass 3: apply. For every collected file that is not part of a collision (and only when dry_run is off), the plugin rewrites dest_path and url component by component. For a component with a file extension, the prefix is removed from the stem and the extension is kept:

dest_path  030--guides/010--setup/index.html  →  guides/setup/index.html
url        030--guides/010--setup/            →  guides/setup/

The trailing / that use_directory_urls: true adds to the URL is kept. With use_directory_urls: false the same rules give guides/setup.html.

docs.title: 3. on_nav: clean navigation titles
docs.text:
If strip_nav_titles is on, the plugin walks the navigation tree recursively. Any item whose title starts with the prefix pattern, or with digits followed by whitespace, gets a cleaned title. A folder named 030--guides arrives here as the section title 030 guides and leaves as guides.

Page titles that MkDocs takes from a page's first # heading are set later, when the page is read, so they are not affected by this step. A page without a heading and without a nav: title keeps a title derived from its filename, for example 010 setup. Give every page a first-level heading to avoid this.

docs.title: 4. on_page_markdown: rewrite links (optional)
docs.text:
If strip_links is on, the plugin runs one regular expression over the Markdown of each page:

\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+\.md(?:#[^)]*)?)\)

For each match, it removes the prefix from the filename part of the target and keeps the folder part and any #anchor:

[Setup](030--guides/010--setup.md#install)  →  [Setup](030--guides/setup.md#install)

This happens before MkDocs resolves links, which is why the option usually breaks links. See Links and navigation.

docs.title: Order relative to other plugins
docs.text: MkDocs runs plugins in the order they are listed under plugins:. The plugin changes dest_path and url in on_files, so plugins listed after it see the clean values. If another plugin builds the navigation or copies pages by path, test both orders.

docs.title: Link to the prefixed filename
docs.text:
Write internal links with the source filename, prefix included, relative to the current page:

See the [setup guide](030--guides/010--setup.md).
Jump to [installing](030--guides/010--setup.md#installing).

MkDocs looks up 030--guides/010--setup.md among the source files, finds it, and writes the URL that the plugin assigned to it, for example guides/setup/. Anchors are kept. mkdocs build --strict reports no warnings.

This is how the pages of this site link to each other. The link Configuration on this page is written as 030--configuration.md and renders as ../configuration/.

docs.title: Do not link to the clean name
docs.text:
A link to guides/setup.md does not work, because no source file has that path:

WARNING -  Doc file 'index.md' contains a link 'guides/setup.md', but the target is not found among documentation files.

mkdocs build --strict treats this warning as an error.

docs.title: Why strip_links: true breaks links
docs.text:
strip_links: true rewrites link targets in the Markdown before MkDocs resolves them. Two things go wrong:

  1. The rewritten filename no longer matches any source file. [Intro](010--intro.md) becomes [Intro](intro.md), and MkDocs cannot find intro.md.
  2. Only the filename is cleaned, not the folders. 030--guides/010--setup.md becomes 030--guides/setup.md, which matches neither the source path nor the clean URL.

A strict build of a page with such links stops:

WARNING -  Doc file 'index.md' contains a link '020--guides/setup.md', but the target is not found among documentation files.

Aborted with 3 warnings in strict mode!

Keep strip_links: false (the default) and link to prefixed filenames.

docs.title: Links from outside the site
docs.text:
URLs that other people bookmark or that you put in a README use the clean form, because that is what the built site serves:

https://example.com/docs/guides/setup/

docs.title: Automatic navigation
docs.text:
Without a nav: key, MkDocs builds the navigation from the folder structure and sorts entries by source filename. Prefixes therefore define the order. index.md comes first in each folder.

  • Section titles come from folder names. MkDocs turns 030--guides into 030 guides, and the plugin cleans it to guides. The plugin does not change the case, so the section appears in lower case.
  • Page titles come from the first # heading of each page.

docs.title: Explicit navigation
docs.text:
With a nav: key you choose the titles yourself and refer to the source paths:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Introduction: 010--introduction.md
  - Guides:
      - Setup: 030--guides/010--setup.md

The plugin still changes the URLs. Titles from nav: have no prefix, so the title cleaning has nothing to do. This site uses an explicit nav:.

docs.title: Edge cases and troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists situations where the result is not obvious, and what to do about them.

docs.title: Filename collisions
docs.text:
A collision happens when two source files have the same path after the prefix is removed:

docs/
├── 010--intro.md   → intro.md
└── 020--intro.md   → intro.md   ← collision

docs.title: With strict: true (default)
docs.text:
The build stops:

ERROR   -  StripNumberPrefix: Multiple files would map to 'intro.md': 010--intro.md, 020--intro.md

Aborted with a BuildError!

The command exits with a non-zero status, so a CI job fails before deployment. To fix it, give the files different names after the prefix:

docs/
├── 010--intro-basics.md     → intro-basics/
└── 020--intro-advanced.md   → intro-advanced/

docs.title: With strict: false
docs.text:
The plugin prints the same message as a warning and continues. Neither colliding file is cleaned; both stay at their prefixed URLs:

site/010--intro/index.html
site/020--intro/index.html

All other pages are cleaned normally. Use this mode only when you accept prefixed URLs for the colliding pages.

docs.title: Folder collisions
docs.text: Folders are cleaned the same way, so 010--guides/index.md and 020--guides/index.md both become guides/index.md and collide. The same strict rules apply.

docs.title: A link warns "target is not found"
docs.text:
WARNING -  Doc file 'index.md' contains a link 'guides/setup.md', but the target is not found among documentation files.

The link uses a clean name. Link to the source filename instead: 030--guides/010--setup.md. If the link was written with a prefix and the warning shows it without one, strip_links: true rewrote it; set strip_links: false. See Links and navigation.

docs.title: Nothing is stripped
docs.text:
Check, in this order:

  1. The plugin is listed under plugins:. A plugins: key replaces MkDocs' default list, so also list search if you want search.
  2. The pattern is written in single quotes with one backslash: pattern: '^\d+--'. The form '^\\d+--' matches nothing in normal filenames.
  3. The pattern matches from the start of each path component. ^\d+-- does not match intro--010.md.
  4. dry_run is false.
  5. The file is a Markdown page. Images, stylesheets and other assets keep their prefixes. Link to them by their real, prefixed path.

docs.title: A navigation entry still shows digits
docs.text: A page with no # heading and no title in nav: gets a title from its filename, for example 010 setup. The plugin cleans titles before MkDocs reads the pages, so this title is not cleaned. Add a first-level heading to the page, or set the title in nav:.

docs.title: Section titles are in lower case
docs.text: MkDocs builds a section title such as 030 guides from the folder name 030--guides. The plugin removes 030 but does not change the case, so the section is shown as guides. Set the title in nav: to control it.

docs.title: verbose or dry_run print nothing
docs.text: The plugin logs through the Python logger mkdocs_strip_number_prefix.plugin. MkDocs only shows messages from the mkdocs logger tree, so the plugin's INFO messages are not shown, even with mkdocs build -v. Warnings are shown, without the WARNING - prefix. To see what dry_run would change, compare the output folder of a build with and without the plugin instead.

docs.title: Zero-padded prefixes such as 00--
docs.text: ^\d+-- matches one or more digits, so 00--, 000-- and 0001-- are all stripped. Files sort by name, so 00--preface.md comes before 010--intro.md. This gives you a slot before the main sequence.

docs.title: A filename that is only a prefix
docs.text: 010--.md has the stem 010--. After stripping, the name is empty and is dropped from the output path, so the page is written to the index.html of its folder. At the top level that overwrites the home page. Always put a name after the prefix: 010--overview.md.

docs.title: The pattern applies per component
docs.text: The pattern is applied to each folder name and the filename separately, never to the whole path. In 010--guides/020--setup.md, the components 010--guides and 020--setup.md are cleaned independently, giving guides/setup.md. A pattern that contains / cannot match.

docs.title: External and non-Markdown links
docs.text: With strip_links: true, only link targets that end in .md (optionally followed by #anchor) are rewritten. https:// links and links to other file types, such as asset.zip, are not touched.

docs.title: Migrating from awesome-pages
docs.text: mkdocs-awesome-pages-plugin and vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix solve related problems in different ways. This page compares them and shows how to switch.

docs.title: What each plugin does
docs.text:
awesome-pages reads a .pages YAML file in each folder to set the order and titles of navigation entries. It does not change URLs:

docs/
├── .pages          # lists intro.md, then guide.md
├── intro.md        → /intro/
└── guide.md        → /guide/

strip-number-prefix takes the order from numeric prefixes in the filenames, which MkDocs already sorts by, and removes the prefixes from the URLs. No extra files are needed:

docs/
├── 010--intro.md   → /intro/
└── 020--guide.md   → /guide/

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Feature awesome-pages strip-number-prefix Control navigation order Yes, in .pages files Yes, through filename prefixes Remove prefixes from URLs No Yes Needs a file per folder Yes (.pages) No Works in subfolders Yes Yes Detects URL collisions No Yes (strict) Cleans section titles from folder names Not applicable Yes (strip_nav_titles)

docs.title: Migration steps
docs.text:
1. Note the order that each .pages file defines.

  2. Rename the files and folders with numeric prefixes in that order. Leave gaps so you can insert pages later:

    git mv docs/intro.md docs/010--intro.md
git mv docs/getting-started docs/020--getting-started

  3. Update internal links to the new filenames, for example [Intro](intro.md) becomes [Intro](010--intro.md). MkDocs resolves them to the clean URLs. See Links and navigation.

  4. Delete the .pages files.

  5. Replace the plugin in mkdocs.yml:

    # Before
plugins:
  - search
  - awesome-pages

# After
plugins:
  - search
  - strip-number-prefix

  6. Build with mkdocs build --strict and check that the URLs in site/ have no prefixes and that there are no link warnings.

The URLs of renamed pages are the same as before, because the prefix is removed again. docs/intro.md was served at /intro/, and docs/010--intro.md is also served at /intro/.

docs.title: Using both plugins
docs.text:
You can keep awesome-pages for features such as custom titles or collapsing, and add strip-number-prefix for the URLs:

plugins:
  - search
  - awesome-pages
  - strip-number-prefix

The two plugins have not been tested together in this repository's test suite. Build with --strict and check the navigation and URLs after adding both.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Contents src/mkdocs_strip_number_prefix/plugin.py The plugin class StripNumberPrefixPlugin src/mkdocs_strip_number_prefix/__init__.py Re-exports the class and __version__ tests/test_plugin.py Unit tests and an end-to-end MkDocs build test src_docs/md/ Source of this documentation (prefixed filenames) src_docs/mkdocs.yml Documentation configuration src_docs/build.sh Builds the documentation into docs/ docs/ Built documentation, served by GitHub Pages build.sh, publish.sh Build and release scripts scripts/ Older helper scripts used by the Makefile

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix
cd vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix

  2. Install the package in editable mode with the development extras:

    python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

    make setup and ./scripts/dev.sh setup do the same through the helper scripts.

  3. Optionally install the pre-commit hooks:

    pre-commit install

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest

or, without a prepared environment:

uvx hatch test

tests/test_plugin.py covers pattern compilation, path cleaning in subfolders, collision handling in both modes, link rewriting, navigation title cleaning and a full MkDocs build. Coverage settings are in pyproject.toml (fail_under = 90 for pytest --cov).

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
ruff check src tests
black src tests
mypy src

make lint and make format wrap these.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
./build.sh docs            # same as the first command

src_docs/build.sh runs ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme through uvx. It installs the plugin from the repository checkout (--with ..), so the documentation is always built with the current source of the plugin. The build is strict: any warning, such as a broken link, fails it.

On every push to main that changes src_docs/, the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml runs the same script and commits the rebuilt docs/ folder. GitHub Pages serves it at https://vexy.dev/vexy-mkdocs-strip-number-prefix/.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package

This removes dist/, runs uv build and checks the result with uvx twine check dist/*. ./build.sh without an argument builds both the documentation and the package.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The version is not written in pyproject.toml. hatch-vcs derives it from the latest git tag at build time and writes it to src/mkdocs_strip_number_prefix/_version.py, which is not committed. A build from the tag v1.0.13 produces version 1.0.13; a build from a later commit produces a development version such as 1.0.14.dev2+g1a2b3c4.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Make sure the tests pass and CHANGELOG.md describes the changes.
  2. Set a PyPI token for uv publish, for example in UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN.

  3. Run:

    ./publish.sh

    publish.sh runs uvx gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes it. It then builds the package from that tag with ./build.sh package and uploads dist/* with uv publish.

Pushing a v* tag also starts .github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with trusted publishing (skip-existing: true, so a version already uploaded by publish.sh does not fail the job) and creates a GitHub release.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository and create a branch.
  2. Add tests for new behaviour in tests/test_plugin.py.
  3. Run the tests and linters.
  4. If the change affects users, update CHANGELOG.md and the pages in src_docs/md/, and run src_docs/build.sh.
  5. Open a pull request.

docs.title: File layouts
docs.text: These layouts show how to number files and what URLs they produce with the default pattern ^\d+--.

docs.title: Sequential numbering
docs.text:
Number in steps of 10 so you can insert pages later without renaming others. Use the same number of digits everywhere, so that names sort correctly: 010, 020, ... 100, not 10, 20, ... 100.

docs/
├── index.md                  → /
├── 010--introduction.md      → /introduction/
├── 020--installation.md      → /installation/
├── 030--configuration.md     → /configuration/
├── 040--advanced.md          → /advanced/
└── 999--troubleshooting.md   → /troubleshooting/

999-- keeps a page at the end however many pages you add.

docs.title: Grouped numbering
docs.text:
Use the hundreds digit for a topic and the tens for pages within it. All files stay in one folder:

docs/
├── 100--getting-started.md   → /getting-started/
├── 110--installation.md      → /installation/
├── 120--first-steps.md       → /first-steps/
├── 200--configuration.md     → /configuration/
├── 210--basic-config.md      → /basic-config/
├── 220--advanced-config.md   → /advanced-config/
└── 900--appendix.md          → /appendix/

docs.title: Numbered folders
docs.text:
Prefix folders as well as files. Both are cleaned:

docs/
├── 010--getting-started/
│   ├── 010--quickstart.md     → /getting-started/quickstart/
│   ├── 020--installation.md   → /getting-started/installation/
│   └── 030--first-steps.md    → /getting-started/first-steps/
├── 020--user-guide/
│   ├── 010--basics.md         → /user-guide/basics/
│   └── 020--configuration.md  → /user-guide/configuration/
└── 030--reference/
    ├── 010--api.md            → /reference/api/
    └── 020--cli.md            → /reference/cli/

Pages in different folders may share a clean name. 010--getting-started/020--installation.md and 020--user-guide/020--installation.md would become getting-started/installation.md and user-guide/installation.md, which do not collide.

docs.title: Mixed: only some files numbered
docs.text:
Unprefixed files are left alone, so you can number only the pages whose order matters:

docs/
├── index.md             → /
├── 010--overview.md     → /overview/
├── 020--tutorial.md     → /tutorial/
├── changelog.md         → /changelog/
└── license.md           → /license/

In the automatic navigation, files are sorted by source name, so the prefixed files (starting with digits) come before changelog.md and license.md.

docs.title: This site
docs.text:
The documentation you are reading is laid out like this:

src_docs/md/
├── index.md
├── 010--installation.md
├── 020--quickstart.md
├── 030--configuration.md
├── 040--how-it-works.md

docs.title: Prefix patterns
docs.text:
The pattern option takes any Python regular expression. It is tested with re.match against each path component, so it only has to describe the start of a name. Starting it with ^ makes that explicit.

Write patterns in single-quoted YAML strings with single backslashes.

docs.title: Common formats
docs.text: Pattern Matches Example source → URL '^\d+--' (default) Any number of digits, then -- 123--file.md → file/ '^\d{3}--' Exactly three digits, then -- 001--file.md → file/ '^\d+-' Digits, then one - 42-file.md → file/ '^\d+_' Digits, then _ 01_file.md → file/ '^[0-9]{2,4}-' Two to four digits, then - 0001-file.md → file/

docs.title: Three-digit prefixes only
docs.text:
plugins:
  - strip-number-prefix:
      pattern: '^\d{3}--'

010--intro.md becomes intro/. 10--intro.md does not match and keeps its prefix in the URL. Use this to make sure all names use the same width.

docs.title: Single-dash prefixes
docs.text:
plugins:
  - strip-number-prefix:
      pattern: '^\d+-'

01-intro.md becomes intro/. Be careful with names that start with a number as part of the title, such as 2024-review.md: it becomes review/. The double dash in the default pattern avoids that.

docs.title: Patterns that end in a dot do not work
docs.text:
plugins:
  - strip-number-prefix:
      pattern: '^\d+\.'   # does not clean URLs

With 1.intro.md, the plugin detects the prefix, but the URLs stay 1.intro/. When the plugin cleans dest_path and url, it treats the text after the last dot of a component as a file extension and applies the pattern to the part before it. For the URL component 1.intro, that part is 1, which does not match ^\d+\.. Use a separator other than ., such as --, - or _.

docs.title: Choosing a pattern
docs.text:
• Keep one pattern for the whole project. The plugin has one pattern option and applies it everywhere.
  • Prefer a separator that does not occur naturally at the start of names. -- is a good choice.
  • After changing the pattern, run mkdocs build --strict. A pattern that is too broad can make two pages collide, and strict mode reports it.
